en.title: Closed-Form Forward Noising
en.readme:
# Closed-Form Forward Noising

## 1. What the paper solves

DDPM gradually transforms complex data into Gaussian noise, then learns to reverse the process. A closed-form forward distribution lets training select any time directly, without simulating every preceding step.

This module selects the closed-form marginal in Equation (4). Implement only `q_sample`; linear schedules, cumulative coefficients, and a cosine comparison schedule are supplied. The cosine schedule comes from Improved DDPM and is included as an optional comparison.

## 2. Core equations

The one-step noise variance is $\beta_t$, the retained signal fraction is $\alpha_t=1-\beta_t$, and the cumulative signal is $\bar\alpha_t=\prod_{s=1}^t\alpha_s$. Independent noise from successive steps combines into a single variance:

$$q(x_t\mid x_0)=\mathcal N(\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}x_0,(1-\bar\alpha_t)I),\qquad x_t=\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}x_0+\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\epsilon.$$

Here $x_0$ and $\epsilon$ have shape `[B,...]`, times t have shape `[B]`, and schedule arrays have shape `[T]`. When data and noise are independent standard Gaussians, the two variance contributions sum to one. The point cloud can therefore keep the same overall scale even as its structure disappears. See the closed-form marginal in [DDPM Equation 4](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.11239).

## 3. From equations to code

Implement only `q_sample(x0, t, noise, alpha_bars)`:

```text
Extract each sample’s cumulative coefficient using its own t
Move coefficients to x0’s dtype/device and reshape to [B,1,...,1]
Combine x0 and noise using the signal and noise standard deviations
```

Return the same shape and dtype as `x0`. Each sample may use a different time; the first row’s time must not control the batch. Noise is supplied by the caller, so this function draws no random numbers.

`linear_betas`, `cosine_betas`, and `make_schedule` are fully implemented. Read them for context; no changes to these helpers are required.

## 4. Conventions

| Item | This exercise | Common implementations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Indexing | Array index i=0 corresponds to paper time t=1 | Papers typically start at 1 |
| Schedule precision | float64 | Extracted coefficients are often converted to float32 during training |
| Linear beta | Fixed endpoints 1e-4 and 0.02 | improved-diffusion scales endpoints by the number of steps |
| Cosine beta | Maximum 0.999 | improved-diffusion also limits the maximum beta |

## 5. Interactive visualizations

<viz id="schedule_curves" />

Adjust the number of steps and offset s to compare cumulative signal and log-SNR for both schedules. A nonzero terminal signal means that a standard Gaussian is only an approximate starting boundary for sampling.

<viz id="forward_cloud" />

Move through time to compare how quickly structure disappears from the same eight-Gaussian data and noise samples. Reusing samples prevents random variation from being mistaken for a schedule effect.

## 6. Run your implementation

Complete the functions in the Python editor on the right, then click **Run tests**. Inspect each failed check, update your implementation, and run again. Passing every required check marks the problem as solved and unlocks the notes.

## 7. Further exploration

The cosine schedule in [Improved DDPM Equation 16](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.09672) is an optional comparison, supplied in `cosine_betas`:

$$f(\tau)=\cos^2\left(\frac{\tau+s}{1+s}\frac\pi2\right),\qquad\beta_i=\min\left(1-\frac{f((i+1)/T)}{f(i/T)},0.999\right).$$

The log signal-to-noise ratio $\log\bar\alpha-\log(1-\bar\alpha)$ helps compare schedules. Continue with “Posterior and Reverse Denoising Step” under the same DDPM paper.
en.notes:
# Forward noising: Review after passing

- The first cumulative alpha is not 1; the first *previous-time* cumulative alpha is 1. `test_reference` and `test_linear_endpoints` catch index shifts.
- Beta is a variance. The multiplier on noise must be a standard deviation. Missing square roots shrink the variance at intermediate times; see `test_variance_preserving`.
- Without clipping, the final cosine beta becomes 1 and can cause division by zero in later inversions. `test_cosine_clip` fixes the upper bound at 0.999.
- Each sample has its own time. Index the schedule with t before expanding spatial dimensions. `test_per_sample_time` uses unsorted, nonconsecutive times so incorrect broadcasting cannot pass by coincidence.

The original exercise checked [Improved DDPM Equation 16](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.09672) and the [official `betas_for_alpha_bar` implementation](https://github.com/openai/improved-diffusion/blob/main/improved_diffusion/gaussian_diffusion.py) on 2026-10-13. The official linear schedule scales endpoints by 1000/T; this exercise keeps them fixed.

# v 参数化与逆变换

## 1. 论文解决什么问题

扩散网络可以预测干净数据、加入的噪声，也可以预测速度。Salimans 与 Ho 在少步蒸馏中研究这些参数化：同一个训练样本，换一种预测目标会改变端点稳定性与误差权重。

本模块精选论文附录 D 中支持少步采样的参数化技术。只需实现 `make_v`、`v_to_x0` 和 `v_to_eps`；其余转换辅助函数已经提供。完成本模块表示掌握这组旋转关系，师生模型、蒸馏目标及逐轮减步训练属于论文的其他内容。

## 2. 核心公式

设 $x_0,\epsilon,x_t\in\mathbb R^{B\times D}$，$\alpha=\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}$、$\sigma=\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}$ 可广播到输入形状，且 $\alpha^2+\sigma^2=1$。本题的 alpha 是标准差系数，和前向加噪模块中单步 alpha 的含义不同。

$$x_t=\alpha x_0+\sigma\epsilon,\qquad v=\alpha\epsilon-\sigma x_0.$$

$$x_0=\alpha x_t-\sigma v,\qquad\epsilon=\sigma x_t+\alpha v.$$

令 $\alpha=\cos\phi,\sigma=\sin\phi$，就能直接求导得到 $v=dx_t/d\phi$。逆变换是二维正交旋转，因而不需要除法。相反，由噪声恢复数据要除以 alpha，由数据恢复噪声要除以 sigma，在各自接近零的端点会放大预测误差。对同一个错误预测，三个表示的误差满足

$$\|\hat v-v\|^2=\frac{\|\hat x_0-x_0\|^2}{\sigma^2}=\frac{\|\hat\epsilon-\epsilon\|^2}{\alpha^2}.$$

这解释了预测目标为何也隐含损失权重。以上旋转关系见 [Progressive Distillation 附录 D，式 26、30](https://arxiv.org/html/2202.00512v2#A4)。

## 3. 从公式到代码

实现三个核心函数：

| 函数 | 输入与输出 | 要点 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `make_v` | `x0, eps, alpha, sigma` → v | 计算旋转的切向量 |
| `v_to_x0` | `x_t, v, alpha, sigma` → x0 | 直接使用逆旋转 |
| `v_to_eps` | `x_t, v, alpha, sigma` → epsilon | 直接使用逆旋转 |

张量形状为 `[B,...]`，系数可广播到该形状。保持输入 shape 和 dtype，不沿 batch 聚合；两项逆变换均无需除法，因而在纯信号与纯噪声端点保持稳定。

`eps_to_x0`、`x0_to_eps` 与 `convert` 已提供。分母下限 `1e-8`、字符串检查和同参数化直接返回都由这些辅助函数处理。`convert` 会调用你实现的三个核心函数。

## 4. 本题约定

| 项目 | 本题 | 常见调度器接口 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 输入系数 | 已开方的 alpha、sigma | 常保存 alpha_cumprod，再在内部开方 |
| 输出 | 直接返回 Tensor | diffusers 调度器通常返回 step 输出对象 |
| 端点除法 | clamp 到 1e-8 | 由具体调度与稳定性策略决定 |
| 数据维度 | 任意可广播形状 | 图像通常使用 B×C×H×W |

## 5. 交互可视化

<viz id="param_circle" />

拖动旋转角 phi，观察位置向量与切向量：切向量的符号由旋转方向决定。这里画的是系数平面；高维独立噪声与数据近似正交时，也可以直观理解为样本平面。

<viz id="error_amplification" />

拖动时间，查看 $1/\alpha$ 和 $1/\sigma$ 的放大系数，理解某个参数化在端点更难训练的原因。

## 6. 在网页中运行

在右侧 Python 编辑器中补全实现，点击 **运行测试**。查看失败测试的原因、期望值与实际值，修改代码后再次运行。所有必要测试通过后，题目会标记为已完成并解锁坑点讲解。

## 7. 延伸

论文的完整方法还包括师生蒸馏与逐轮缩减采样步数，可继续阅读 [Progressive Distillation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.00512)。Flow Matching 使用对线性时间求导的另一种速度，与这里对旋转角求导的 v 不应混用。
problems.notes:
# 通过后的复盘

- v 符号反转时，shape 完全正常，但运动方向相反。`test_velocity_tangent` 用有限差分确定正确符号。
- alpha 是累计信号的平方根；多平方一次会在高噪声时放大误差。`test_six_roundtrips` 和 `test_reference` 定位这类错误。
- alpha=0 时噪声无法唯一决定 x0；clamp 只保证有限值，不创造缺失的信息。v 的逆旋转仍精确，见 `test_endpoint_stability`。
- 不同参数化损失隐含不同时间权重。`test_error_weight_identity` 将同一错误预测统一到三种表示，避免比较无关的预测误差。

已核对 [Salimans & Ho 附录 D，式 26、30](https://arxiv.org/html/2202.00512v2#A4)，访问日期 2026-10-13。

en.title: v-Parameterization and Inverse Rotation
en.readme:
# v-Parameterization and Inverse Rotation

## 1. What the paper solves

A diffusion network can predict clean data, added noise, or velocity. Salimans and Ho study these parameterizations for distillation into fewer sampling steps. Changing the prediction target for the same training sample changes endpoint stability and the weighting of prediction errors.

This module selects the supporting parameterization technique from Appendix D. Implement only `make_v`, `v_to_x0`, and `v_to_eps`; the other conversion helpers are supplied. Completing this module covers these rotation identities. Teacher–student targets and progressive training remain separate parts of the paper.

## 2. Core equations

Let $x_0,\epsilon,x_t\in\mathbb R^{B\times D}$, with $\alpha=\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}$ and $\sigma=\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}$ broadcastable to the input shape, and $\alpha^2+\sigma^2=1$. Here alpha is a square-root signal coefficient, unlike the one-step alpha in problem **6**.

$$x_t=\alpha x_0+\sigma\epsilon,\qquad v=\alpha\epsilon-\sigma x_0.$$

$$x_0=\alpha x_t-\sigma v,\qquad\epsilon=\sigma x_t+\alpha v.$$

Set $\alpha=\cos\phi$ and $\sigma=\sin\phi$; differentiation gives $v=dx_t/d\phi$. The inverse is a two-dimensional orthogonal rotation and requires no division. In contrast, recovering data from noise divides by alpha, while recovering noise from data divides by sigma. Each amplifies prediction errors near the endpoint where its denominator approaches zero. For the same erroneous prediction expressed in all three representations:

$$\|\hat v-v\|^2=\frac{\|\hat x_0-x_0\|^2}{\sigma^2}=\frac{\|\hat\epsilon-\epsilon\|^2}{\alpha^2}.$$

The prediction target therefore also implies a loss weighting. See [Progressive Distillation, Appendix D, Equations 26 and 30](https://arxiv.org/html/2202.00512v2#A4).

## 3. From equations to code

Implement three core functions:

| Function | Inputs and output | Key idea |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `make_v` | `x0, eps, alpha, sigma` → v | Compute the rotation’s tangent |
| `v_to_x0` | `x_t, v, alpha, sigma` → x0 | Apply the inverse rotation directly |
| `v_to_eps` | `x_t, v, alpha, sigma` → epsilon | Apply the inverse rotation directly |

Tensors have shape `[B,...]`; coefficients broadcast to that shape. Preserve shape and dtype without aggregating over the batch. Neither inverse requires division, preserving stability at the pure-signal and pure-noise endpoints.

`eps_to_x0`, `x0_to_eps`, and `convert` are provided. They handle the `1e-8` denominator floor, string validation, and identity conversions. `convert` calls your three core functions.

## 4. Conventions

| Item | This exercise | Common scheduler interfaces |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Input coefficients | Already square-rooted alpha and sigma | Often store alpha_cumprod and take square roots internally |
| Output | Return a Tensor directly | diffusers schedulers usually return a step-output object |
| Endpoint division | Clamp denominator to 1e-8 | Depends on the schedule and stability strategy |
| Data dimensions | Any broadcastable shape | Images usually use B×C×H×W |

## 5. Interactive visualizations

<viz id="param_circle" />

Adjust the rotation angle phi to inspect the position and tangent vectors. The rotation direction determines the tangent's sign. This plot shows the coefficient plane; when high-dimensional independent noise and data are approximately orthogonal, it also suggests a sample-space interpretation.

<viz id="error_amplification" />

Move through time to inspect amplification factors $1/\alpha$ and $1/\sigma$, and understand why a parameterization becomes harder near an endpoint.

## 6. Run your implementation

Complete the functions in the Python editor on the right, then click **Run tests**. Inspect each failed check, update your implementation, and run again. Passing every required check marks the problem as solved and unlocks the notes.

## 7. Further exploration

For teacher–student targets and progressive step reduction, continue reading [Progressive Distillation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.00512). Flow Matching uses a different velocity, differentiated with respect to linear time; this module differentiates with respect to a rotation angle.
en.notes:
# Parameterization conversion: Review after passing

- Reversing v's sign preserves every shape but reverses motion. `test_velocity_tangent` determines the correct sign with finite differences.
- Alpha is the square root of cumulative signal. Squaring it again amplifies errors at high noise levels. `test_six_roundtrips` and `test_reference` catch this mistake.
- At alpha=0, noise cannot uniquely determine x0. Clamping produces finite values but cannot recover missing information. The inverse rotation from v remains exact; see `test_endpoint_stability`.
- Losses for different parameterizations imply different time weights. `test_error_weight_identity` converts the same erroneous prediction into all three representations, avoiding comparisons between unrelated prediction errors.

The original exercise checked [Salimans and Ho, Appendix D, Equations 26 and 30](https://arxiv.org/html/2202.00512v2#A4) on 2026-10-13.

problems.readme:
# 后验与反向去噪一步

## 1. 论文解决什么问题

DDPM 将生成过程拆成许多小的去噪步骤。训练时可解析的高斯后验提供学习目标，采样时网络预测的噪声决定每一步往哪里走。

这是 DDPM 论文的第二个核心模块。只需实现 `q_posterior` 与 `p_sample_step`，把解析后验和噪声预测接成一次反向更新。完整采样循环 `ddpm_sample` 与测试使用的噪声预测器已经提供。

## 2. 核心公式

已知干净数据后，$q(x_{t-1}\mid x_t,x_0)$ 是高斯。它的均值由当前样本与干净数据的加权和组成：

$$\tilde\mu_t=\frac{\sqrt{\bar\alpha_{t-1}}\beta_t}{1-\bar\alpha_t}x_0+\frac{\sqrt{1-\beta_t}(1-\bar\alpha_{t-1})}{1-\bar\alpha_t}x_t,\qquad\tilde\beta_t=\frac{1-\bar\alpha_{t-1}}{1-\bar\alpha_t}\beta_t.$$

网络看不到真实 x0，因此先由噪声预测恢复它：

$$\hat x_0=\frac{x_t-\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\hat\epsilon}{\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}},\qquad x_{t-1}=\tilde\mu_t(x_t,\hat x_0)+\sigma_tz.$$

$x_t,\hat\epsilon,z$ 都是 `[B,...]`，t 是 `[B]`，每一行可以选择不同时间。方差是 `[B,1,...]`，由广播扩展到样本。后验及噪声参数化见 [DDPM 式 6、7、11 与算法 2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.11239)。

本题将网络换成八高斯混合分布的精确 score，得到 $\epsilon^*=-\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\nabla\log p_t$。因此无需训练，也能检验采样结果是否恢复原分布。输出仍有有限步离散化和有限样本误差，不能期待经验 MMD 恰好为零。

## 3. 从公式到代码

实现两个核心函数：

```text
q_posterior: 按 [B] 时间提取系数，组合 x0 与 x_t，返回均值和方差
p_sample_step: 从 epsilon 预测恢复 x0，调用 q_posterior
按 var_type 选择 posterior 或 beta 方差
把 t=0 的噪声贡献置零，得到更新后的样本
```

`q_posterior` 返回均值 `[B,...]` 和可广播的方差 `[B,1,...]`。`p_sample_step` 返回与 `x_t` 同形状、同 dtype 的张量。未知 `var_type` 抛出 `ValueError`。

`_extract` 和 `ddpm_sample` 已提供。后者管理初始高斯噪声、降序时间循环、调用者的 generator 与轨迹记录；每一步都会调用你的 `p_sample_step`。`return_traj=True` 时返回 `(samples, trajectory)`，轨迹 `[T+1,B,...]` 包含初始噪声。

## 4. 本题约定

| 项目 | 本题 | improved-diffusion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| x0 范围 | 二维数据不裁剪 | 图像常裁剪到 [-1,1] |
| 方差选项 | posterior 或 beta | 还支持网络学习方差 |
| 最后一步 | 两种选项均不加噪 | 同样屏蔽最终噪声 |
| 首个 log 方差 | 不计算 log 方差 | 用下一项方差填充后取 log |

## 5. 交互可视化

<viz id="reverse_particles" />

播放反向轨迹，切换 posterior 与 beta 方差，观察粒子从噪声聚集到八个模式；灰色中心表示真实数据位置。

<viz id="variance_compare" />

拖动时间比较 beta 与后验方差，最后一步两者差异最大，但都必须停止注入噪声。运行测试后，结果面板可叠加采样点、真实样本以及 MMD 阈值。

## 6. 在网页中运行

在右侧 Python 编辑器中补全实现，点击 **运行测试**。查看失败测试的原因、期望值与实际值，修改代码后再次运行。所有必要测试通过后，题目会标记为已完成并解锁坑点讲解。

## 7. 延伸

下一题 DDIM 保留同一个噪声预测器，却能沿时间子序列跳步。想研究学习方差，可继续阅读 [Improved DDPM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.09672)。

problems.solution:
"""Ancestral DDPM sampling with a caller-supplied epsilon predictor."""
import torch
from torch import Tensor
from typing import Callable


def _extract(values, t, x):
    return values.to(x)[t].reshape(-1, *([1] * (x.ndim - 1)))


def q_posterior(x0: Tensor, x_t: Tensor, t: Tensor, betas: Tensor, alpha_bars: Tensor,
                alpha_bars_prev: Tensor) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    """Return posterior mean [B,...] and broadcastable variance [B,1,...]."""
    beta = _extract(betas, t, x_t)
    ab, prev = _extract(alpha_bars, t, x_t), _extract(alpha_bars_prev, t, x_t)
    c0 = prev.sqrt() * beta / (1 - ab)
    ct = (1 - beta).sqrt() * (1 - prev) / (1 - ab)
    mean = c0 * x0 + ct * x_t
    var = beta * (1 - prev) / (1 - ab)
    return mean, var


def p_sample_step(eps_pred: Tensor, x_t: Tensor, t: Tensor, betas: Tensor,
                  alpha_bars: Tensor, alpha_bars_prev: Tensor, noise: Tensor,
                  var_type: str = "posterior") -> Tensor:
    """Use posterior or beta variance; samples with index t=0 receive no noise."""
    ab = _extract(alpha_bars, t, x_t)
    x0 = (x_t - (1 - ab).sqrt() * eps_pred) / ab.sqrt()
    mean, var = q_posterior(x0, x_t, t, betas, alpha_bars, alpha_bars_prev)
    if var_type == "beta":
        var = _extract(betas, t, x_t)
    elif var_type != "posterior":
        raise ValueError("var_type must be posterior or beta")
    nonzero = (t != 0).to(x_t).reshape(-1, *([1] * (x_t.ndim - 1)))
    return mean + nonzero * var.clamp(min=0).sqrt() * noise


@torch.no_grad()
def ddpm_sample(eps_model: Callable[[Tensor, Tensor], Tensor], shape: tuple[int, ...], betas: Tensor, generator: torch.Generator, var_type: str = "posterior", return_traj: bool = False) -> Tensor | tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    """Start at N(0,I), traverse T-1..0; optionally return (samples, [T+1,B,...])."""
    ab = (1 - betas).cumprod(0)
    prev = torch.cat((torch.ones_like(ab[:1]), ab[:-1]))
    x = torch.randn(shape, dtype=betas.dtype, device=betas.device, generator=generator)
    trajectory = [x.clone()] if return_traj else None
    for step in reversed(range(len(betas))):
        t = torch.full((shape[0],), step, dtype=torch.long, device=x.device)
        noise = torch.randn(x.shape, dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device, generator=generator)
        x = p_sample_step(eps_model(x, t), x, t, betas, ab, prev, noise, var_type)
        if return_traj:
            trajectory.append(x.clone())
    return (x, torch.stack(trajectory)) if return_traj else x
problems.notes:
# 通过后的复盘

- 后验均值两项长得相近，却不能交换。`test_precision_product` 用高斯精度相加独立推导均值与方差，不依赖参考实现。
- 首个后验方差严格为零。improved-diffusion 在计算 log 方差前用第二项替换首项，避免 log(0)；本题直接使用方差，无需这一处理。[官方源码](https://github.com/openai/improved-diffusion/blob/main/improved_diffusion/gaussian_diffusion.py) 于 2026-10-13 核对。
- 最后一步不加噪对 beta 方差选项也成立。只测试 posterior 会漏掉这一错误，`test_last_step_no_noise` 同时检查两种选项。
- 图像中的 x0 clipping 不能直接照搬到半径为 2 的点云。`test_gmm_sampling` 检查八个模式而非只检查点云中心。
- 采样必须降序；`test_sampler_time_order` 给出准确的错误时间位置，T3 再从分布层面检查。T3 MMD 阈值为参考实测的 1.5 倍，模式占比 12.5%±3%，半径 .5 外样本少于 5%。

en.title: Posterior and Reverse Denoising Step
en.readme:
# Posterior and Reverse Denoising Step

## 1. What the paper solves

DDPM decomposes generation into many small denoising steps. An analytic Gaussian posterior supplies a training target; at sampling time, predicted noise determines where each step moves.

This is the second selected core module of DDPM. Implement only `q_posterior` and `p_sample_step`, connecting the analytic posterior and noise prediction into one reverse update. The full `ddpm_sample` loop and the test noise predictor are supplied.

## 2. Core equations

Given the clean data, $q(x_{t-1}\mid x_t,x_0)$ is Gaussian. Its mean is a weighted combination of the current sample and clean data:

$$\tilde\mu_t=\frac{\sqrt{\bar\alpha_{t-1}}\beta_t}{1-\bar\alpha_t}x_0+\frac{\sqrt{1-\beta_t}(1-\bar\alpha_{t-1})}{1-\bar\alpha_t}x_t,\qquad\tilde\beta_t=\frac{1-\bar\alpha_{t-1}}{1-\bar\alpha_t}\beta_t.$$

The network cannot observe the true x0, so first reconstruct it from the noise prediction:

$$\hat x_0=\frac{x_t-\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\hat\epsilon}{\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t}},\qquad x_{t-1}=\tilde\mu_t(x_t,\hat x_0)+\sigma_tz.$$

$x_t$, $\hat\epsilon$, and $z$ have shape `[B,...]`; t has shape `[B]`, allowing a different time for each row. The variance has shape `[B,1,...]` and broadcasts to the sample. See [DDPM Equations 6, 7, and 11, and Algorithm 2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.11239).

This exercise replaces the network with the exact score of an eight-component Gaussian mixture, giving $\epsilon^*=-\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}\nabla\log p_t$. Sampling quality can then be checked without training. Finite-step discretization and finite-sample error remain, so empirical MMD need not equal zero.

## 3. From equations to code

Implement two core functions:

```text
q_posterior: extract coefficients at [B] times; combine x0 and x_t
Return the posterior mean and variance
p_sample_step: recover x0 from epsilon, then call q_posterior
Choose posterior or beta variance according to var_type
Zero the noise contribution wherever t=0 and return the updated sample
```

`q_posterior` returns a mean of shape `[B,...]` and broadcastable variance `[B,1,...]`. `p_sample_step` returns the shape and dtype of `x_t`. Raise `ValueError` for an unknown `var_type`.

`_extract` and `ddpm_sample` are supplied. The sampler handles initial Gaussian noise, descending times, the caller’s generator, and trajectory collection; each update calls your `p_sample_step`. With `return_traj=True`, it returns `(samples, trajectory)` with shape `[T+1,B,...]` including initial noise.

## 4. Conventions

| Item | This exercise | improved-diffusion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| x0 range | No clipping for two-dimensional data | Images are often clipped to [-1,1] |
| Variance options | posterior or beta | Also supports learned variance |
| Final step | No added noise under either option | Also masks the final noise |
| First log variance | No log variance is computed | Replaces the first variance with the next value before taking logs |

## 5. Interactive visualizations

<viz id="reverse_particles" />

Play the reverse trajectory and switch between posterior and beta variance. Observe particles move from noise into eight modes; gray centers mark the true data locations.

<viz id="variance_compare" />

Move through time to compare beta and posterior variance. Their final-step difference is greatest, but both options must stop adding noise there. After running your implementation, the results panel can overlay generated points, true samples, and the MMD threshold.

## 6. Run your implementation

Complete the functions in the Python editor on the right, then click **Run tests**. Inspect each failed check, update your implementation, and run again. Passing every required check marks the problem as solved and unlocks the notes.

## 7. Further exploration

DDIM reuses the same noise predictor while skipping along a subsequence of times. For learned variance, continue with [Improved DDPM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.09672).

# DDPM sampling: Review after passing

- The two posterior-mean coefficients look similar but are not interchangeable. `test_precision_product` derives mean and variance independently by adding Gaussian precisions, without relying on the reference implementation.
- The first posterior variance is exactly zero. improved-diffusion replaces it with the second entry before computing log variance to avoid log(0). This exercise uses variance directly, so no replacement is needed. The original exercise checked the [official implementation](https://github.com/openai/improved-diffusion/blob/main/improved_diffusion/gaussian_diffusion.py) on 2026-10-13.
- The final step must omit noise for beta variance too. Testing only posterior variance can miss this mistake; `test_last_step_no_noise` checks both options.
- Copying image x0 clipping into a point cloud of radius 2 damages the distribution. `test_gmm_sampling` checks all eight modes, rather than only the overall center.
- Sampling must visit times in descending order. `test_sampler_time_order` identifies the exact incorrect position; T3 checks the resulting distribution. Its MMD threshold is 1.5 times the measured reference value, each mode's target share is 12.5%±3%, and fewer than 5% of samples may lie more than .5 from a mode center.

problems.readme:
# DDIM 跳步更新

## 1. 论文解决什么问题

DDPM 的训练目标只要求各时间的边缘加噪分布，并没有把采样轨迹唯一固定。DDIM 利用这一自由度复用已有噪声预测器，以更少的去噪步骤生成样本。

本模块只要求实现 `ddim_step`，直接抓住论文的跳步更新公式。时间子序列和完整采样循环已经提供；反演辅助代码与可视化保留为可选探索。

## 2. 核心公式

设当前累计信号为 $a=\bar\alpha_t$，前一个采样时间的累计信号为 $b=\bar\alpha_{\mathrm{prev}}$，因此 $b\ge a$。先恢复干净预测，再组合确定性方向与随机噪声：

$$\hat x_0=\frac{x_t-\sqrt{1-a}\hat\epsilon}{\sqrt a},\qquad\sigma=\eta\sqrt{\frac{1-b}{1-a}}\sqrt{1-\frac ab}.$$

$$x_{\mathrm{prev}}=\sqrt b\hat x_0+\sqrt{1-b-\sigma^2}\hat\epsilon+\sigma z.$$

所有样本张量为 `[B,D]`；a、b 可以是标量，也可广播到样本形状。eta 等于零时，每一条轨迹由初始噪声唯一确定；eta 等于一且相邻时间步时，随机方差与 DDPM 后验相同。这里必须从方向项中扣掉随机项的方差，否则总噪声会过量。更新和 eta 参数化分别见 [DDIM 式 12、16](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.02502)。

最后一次更新设置 b=1，把样本送到真正的干净端点。单点分布是很强的检查：完美 x0 预测下，无论采样一步还是五十步，都应精确到达该点。

## 3. 从公式到代码

只实现 `ddim_step(x_t, eps_pred, ab_t, ab_prev, eta, noise)`：

```text
用当前 ab_t 与 epsilon 预测恢复 x0
从当前和目标累计系数计算 sigma
从方向项方差中扣除 sigma²
组合 x0 预测、epsilon 方向和调用者提供的噪声
```

返回与 `x_t` 同形状、同 dtype 的张量。`ab_t` 与 `ab_prev` 可广播到样本；最终干净端点使用 `ab_prev=1`，此时方向项和随机项都消失。`eta=0` 时输出与传入噪声无关。

`ddim_timesteps` 和 `ddim_sample` 已提供。采样循环会对每一对时间调用你的 `ddim_step`，并可返回包含起点与终点的 `[n+1,B,D]` 轨迹。`ddim_invert` 也已提供，用于可选的往返实验，无需自行实现。

## 4. 本题约定

| 项目 | 本题 | diffusers DDIMScheduler |
| --- | --- | --- |
| trailing 步距 | T 整除 n | 实数 T/n 后取整 |
| T 能整除 n 时 | 两者相同 | 两者相同 |
| 其他选项 | 仅固定 trailing | 另有 leading、linspace |
| 干净边界 | 最后 b=1 | set_alpha_to_one 控制 |

表格按 [官方调度器源码](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/main/src/diffusers/schedulers/scheduling_ddim.py) 于 2026-10-13 核对。非整除情况优先遵循本题定义。

## 5. 交互可视化

<viz id="eta_steps_grid" />

点击 eta 与步数组合，播放同一初始噪声的轨迹并比较最终 MMD，观察随机性与计算预算的关系。

<viz id="inversion_demo" />

选择数据点与步数，查看反演噪声、重建位置及往返误差；网格更密时通常更接近原样本。

## 6. 在网页中运行

在右侧 Python 编辑器中补全实现，点击 **运行测试**。查看失败测试的原因、期望值与实际值，修改代码后再次运行。所有必要测试通过后，题目会标记为已完成并解锁坑点讲解。

## 7. 延伸

提供的反演是一阶近似：从干净端点出发时首次使用索引零，之后在当前位置和时间求 epsilon。有限步数下，它通常不是非线性采样映射的精确代数逆。可用反演可视化比较不同步数的往返误差；这部分无需补全代码。少步误差还可参考 [Progressive Distillation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.00512)。

Required: ddim_step.
Provided: ddim_timesteps, ddim_sample, ddim_invert.
"""
import torch
from torch import Tensor
from typing import Callable


# Core implementation
def ddim_step(x_t: Tensor, eps_pred: Tensor, ab_t: Tensor, ab_prev: Tensor,
              eta: float, noise: Tensor) -> Tensor:
    """Coefficients broadcast to x_t; final ab_prev=1."""
    # TODO: implement the selected core module.
    raise NotImplementedError


# Provided helpers
def ddim_timesteps(T: int, num_steps: int) -> Tensor:
    """[num_steps] long: T-1-k*(T//num_steps), strict descending."""
    if not 1 <= num_steps <= T:
        raise ValueError("num_steps must lie in [1,T]")
    return T - 1 - torch.arange(num_steps, dtype=torch.long) * (T // num_steps)

@torch.no_grad()
def ddim_sample(eps_model: Callable[[Tensor, Tensor], Tensor], x_T: Tensor, alpha_bars: Tensor, num_steps: int, eta: float = 0.0, generator: torch.Generator | None = None, return_traj: bool = False) -> Tensor | tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    """Return samples or (samples, trajectory including x_T and clean endpoint)."""
    steps = ddim_timesteps(len(alpha_bars), num_steps).tolist()
    ab = alpha_bars.to(x_T)
    x = x_T.clone()
    trajectory = [x.clone()] if return_traj else None
    for i, step in enumerate(steps):
        previous = ab[steps[i + 1]] if i + 1 < len(steps) else torch.ones_like(ab[0])
        t = torch.full((len(x),), step, dtype=torch.long, device=x.device)
        noise = torch.randn(x.shape, generator=generator, dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device) if eta else torch.zeros_like(x)
        x = ddim_step(x, eps_model(x, t), ab[step], previous, eta, noise)
        if return_traj:
            trajectory.append(x.clone())
    return (x, torch.stack(trajectory)) if return_traj else x

@torch.no_grad()
def ddim_invert(eps_model: Callable[[Tensor, Tensor], Tensor], x0: Tensor, alpha_bars: Tensor, num_steps: int) -> Tensor:
    """First-order deterministic inversion; evaluate eps at the current time."""
    steps = ddim_timesteps(len(alpha_bars), num_steps).flip(0).tolist()
    ab = alpha_bars.to(x0)
    x = x0.clone()
    current_ab = torch.ones_like(ab[0])
    current_step = 0
    for step in steps:
        t = torch.full((len(x),), current_step, dtype=torch.long, device=x.device)
        eps = eps_model(x, t)
        clean = (x - (1 - current_ab).sqrt() * eps) / current_ab.sqrt()
        x = ab[step].sqrt() * clean + (1 - ab[step]).sqrt() * eps
        current_ab, current_step = ab[step], step
    return x

"""DDIM with explicit trailing subsequences and a clean final boundary."""
import torch
from torch import Tensor
from typing import Callable


def ddim_step(x_t: Tensor, eps_pred: Tensor, ab_t: Tensor, ab_prev: Tensor,
              eta: float, noise: Tensor) -> Tensor:
    """Coefficients broadcast to x_t; final ab_prev=1."""
    x0 = (x_t - (1 - ab_t).sqrt() * eps_pred) / ab_t.sqrt()
    sigma = eta * ((1 - ab_prev) / (1 - ab_t)).sqrt() * (1 - ab_t / ab_prev).clamp(min=0).sqrt()
    direction = (1 - ab_prev - sigma.square()).clamp(min=0).sqrt()
    return ab_prev.sqrt() * x0 + direction * eps_pred + sigma * noise


def ddim_timesteps(T: int, num_steps: int) -> Tensor:
    """[num_steps] long: T-1-k*(T//num_steps), strict descending."""
    if not 1 <= num_steps <= T:
        raise ValueError("num_steps must lie in [1,T]")
    return T - 1 - torch.arange(num_steps, dtype=torch.long) * (T // num_steps)


@torch.no_grad()
def ddim_sample(eps_model: Callable[[Tensor, Tensor], Tensor], x_T: Tensor, alpha_bars: Tensor, num_steps: int, eta: float = 0.0, generator: torch.Generator | None = None, return_traj: bool = False) -> Tensor | tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    """Return samples or (samples, trajectory including x_T and clean endpoint)."""
    steps = ddim_timesteps(len(alpha_bars), num_steps).tolist()
    ab = alpha_bars.to(x_T)
    x = x_T.clone()
    trajectory = [x.clone()] if return_traj else None
    for i, step in enumerate(steps):
        previous = ab[steps[i + 1]] if i + 1 < len(steps) else torch.ones_like(ab[0])
        t = torch.full((len(x),), step, dtype=torch.long, device=x.device)
        noise = torch.randn(x.shape, generator=generator, dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device) if eta else torch.zeros_like(x)
        x = ddim_step(x, eps_model(x, t), ab[step], previous, eta, noise)
        if return_traj:
            trajectory.append(x.clone())
    return (x, torch.stack(trajectory)) if return_traj else x


@torch.no_grad()
def ddim_invert(eps_model: Callable[[Tensor, Tensor], Tensor], x0: Tensor, alpha_bars: Tensor, num_steps: int) -> Tensor:
    """First-order deterministic inversion; evaluate eps at the current time."""
    steps = ddim_timesteps(len(alpha_bars), num_steps).flip(0).tolist()
    ab = alpha_bars.to(x0)
    x = x0.clone()
    current_ab = torch.ones_like(ab[0])
    current_step = 0
    for step in steps:
        t = torch.full((len(x),), current_step, dtype=torch.long, device=x.device)

# 通过后的复盘

- eta=1 恢复的是相邻时间的后验方差；方向项必须同步减去 sigma²。`test_eta_one_posterior` 和 `test_reference` 分别抓两个因子错误。
- 时间子序列最后一项通常不是 0，数组索引 0 也仍对应一次加噪。必须额外跳到 alpha_bar=1，见 `test_point_final_jump`。
- 本题 trailing 步距是 T//n。diffusers 官方 trailing 使用 T/n 后取整，T=1000、n=50 时一致，非整除时可能不同。`test_trailing_times` 明确覆盖 T=17、n=5。[官方源码](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/main/src/diffusers/schedulers/scheduling_ddim.py) 于 2026-10-13 核对。
- 确定性不表示有限步反演严格可逆：epsilon 依赖当前状态，一阶反演只是局部近似。干净起点首次用索引零近似，`test_inversion_converges` 检验 10→100 步误差下降。
- `test_step_convergence` 固定同一初始噪声，避免把采样随机性误当离散化误差。50 步 eta=1 的对照仅展示，不影响 eta=0 的质量评分。

en.title: DDIM Subsequence Update
en.readme:
# DDIM Subsequence Update

## 1. What the paper solves

DDPM's training objective specifies noisy marginal distributions at each time without uniquely determining sampling trajectories. DDIM uses this freedom to reuse an existing noise predictor and generate samples in fewer denoising steps.

Implement only `ddim_step`, the paper’s central update across a timestep subsequence. Timestep selection and the full sampling loop are supplied. Inversion helpers and visualizations remain available for optional exploration.

## 2. Core equations

Let the current cumulative signal be $a=\bar\alpha_t$ and the previous sampling time's cumulative signal be $b=\bar\alpha_{\mathrm{prev}}$, with $b\ge a$. Reconstruct the clean prediction, then combine a deterministic direction and random noise:

$$\hat x_0=\frac{x_t-\sqrt{1-a}\hat\epsilon}{\sqrt a},\qquad\sigma=\eta\sqrt{\frac{1-b}{1-a}}\sqrt{1-\frac ab}.$$

$$x_{\mathrm{prev}}=\sqrt b\hat x_0+\sqrt{1-b-\sigma^2}\hat\epsilon+\sigma z.$$

Sample tensors have shape `[B,D]`; a and b may be scalars or broadcastable to the sample shape. At eta=0, initial noise uniquely determines the trajectory. At eta=1 with adjacent timesteps, the stochastic variance equals the DDPM posterior variance. Subtract the stochastic variance from the direction term to avoid adding too much total noise. See [DDIM Equations 12 and 16](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.02502) for the update and eta parameterization.

Set b=1 on the final update to reach the true clean endpoint. A point distribution provides a strong check: with perfect x0 predictions, both one step and fifty steps should arrive exactly at the point.

## 3. From equations to code

Implement only `ddim_step(x_t, eps_pred, ab_t, ab_prev, eta, noise)`:

```text
Recover x0 from the current ab_t and epsilon prediction
Compute sigma from the current and target cumulative coefficients
Subtract sigma² from the direction variance
Combine the clean prediction, epsilon direction, and supplied noise
```

Return the shape and dtype of `x_t`. `ab_t` and `ab_prev` broadcast to the sample. The final clean endpoint uses `ab_prev=1`, eliminating both the direction and random terms. With `eta=0`, the result is independent of the supplied noise.

`ddim_timesteps` and `ddim_sample` are provided. The sampler calls your `ddim_step` for each pair of times and can return a `[n+1,B,D]` trajectory including both endpoints. `ddim_invert` is also supplied for optional round-trip experiments; you do not need to implement it.

## 4. Conventions

| Item | This exercise | diffusers DDIMScheduler |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trailing step spacing | Integer spacing T//n | Uses real-valued T/n before rounding |
| When T is divisible by n | The two sequences agree | The two sequences agree |
| Other options | Fixed trailing spacing only | Also supports leading and linspace |
| Clean boundary | Final b=1 | Controlled by set_alpha_to_one |

The original exercise checked this comparison against the [official scheduler source](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/main/src/diffusers/schedulers/scheduling_ddim.py) on 2026-10-13. Follow this exercise's definition when T is not divisible by n.

## 5. Interactive visualizations

<viz id="eta_steps_grid" />

Choose an eta and step-count combination. Play trajectories from the same initial noise and compare final MMD to inspect the relationship between randomness and computation.

<viz id="inversion_demo" />

Choose a data point and step count to inspect inverted noise, reconstructed positions, and round-trip error. A finer time grid usually brings the reconstruction closer to the original sample.

## 6. Run your implementation

Complete the functions in the Python editor on the right, then click **Run tests**. Inspect each failed check, update your implementation, and run again. Passing every required check marks the problem as solved and unlocks the notes.

## 7. Further exploration

The supplied inversion is a first-order approximation. Its first call from the clean endpoint uses index zero; later calls evaluate epsilon at the current state and time. At finite step counts, it is generally not the exact algebraic inverse of a nonlinear sampling map. Compare round-trip errors in the visualization without implementing additional code. For few-step error, see [Progressive Distillation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.00512).
en.notes:
# DDIM: Review after passing

- Eta=1 recovers the posterior variance for adjacent times. The direction term must also subtract sigma². `test_eta_one_posterior` and `test_reference` catch errors in these factors.
- A timestep subsequence usually does not end at index 0, and index 0 itself still represents one noising step. Take an additional jump to alpha_bar=1; see `test_point_final_jump`.
- This exercise uses trailing spacing T//n. The official diffusers trailing sequence uses T/n followed by rounding. They agree for T=1000, n=50 but may differ when division is inexact. `test_trailing_times` explicitly covers T=17, n=5. The original exercise checked the [official source](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/main/src/diffusers/schedulers/scheduling_ddim.py) on 2026-10-13.
- Determinism does not imply exact finite-step invertibility. Epsilon depends on the current state, and first-order inversion is a local approximation. At the clean starting point, it first uses index zero. `test_inversion_converges` checks that error falls when increasing from 10 to 100 steps.
- `test_step_convergence` fixes the initial noise so sampling randomness cannot be mistaken for discretization error. The fifty-step eta=1 comparison is display-only and does not affect the eta=0 quality score.

problems.readme:
# 条件路径与速度回归

## 1. 论文解决什么问题

Flow Matching 学习一个随时间变化的速度场，用常微分方程把噪声搬运到数据。条件训练目标允许直接回归可计算的速度，不必在每次训练时模拟整条生成轨迹。

本模块精选线性条件路径及其 CFM 目标。只需实现 `interpolate`、`cfm_target`、`cfm_loss`；时间采样、Euler 求解器、测试模型和训练循环已经提供。

## 2. 核心公式

本题固定 x0 是噪声，x1 是数据。二者均为 `[B,D]`，时间 t 为 `[B]`，每个样本拥有自己的插值比例：

$$x_t=(1-t)x_0+tx_1,\qquad u=x_1-x_0,\qquad\mathcal L=\operatorname{mean}_{b,d}\left(v_\theta(x_t,t)-u\right)^2.$$

条件速度 u 是一对端点之间的位移，但网络只看见当前位置和时间。同一位置可能由不同端点对产生，因此它学到的是条件速度的平均值。即使网络达到最优，训练损失一般仍不为零；不可约方差不等于实现错误。梯度等价性及线性条件路径见 [Flow Matching 式 5、9、22、23](https://arxiv.org/html/2210.02747v2)。

单点数据是特殊情况：$v^*(x,t)=(\mu-x)/(1-t)$，代入插值即可得到恒定目标速度，因此 oracle loss 为零，Euler 一步也能到达数据点。一般混合分布的边缘轨迹会弯曲，多步求解才有意义。

## 3. 从公式到代码

实现三个围绕同一训练目标的函数：

```text
interpolate: 将 t [B] 广播到 [B,...]，构造噪声到数据的线性路径
cfm_target: 返回这条路径对时间的导数
cfm_loss: 在 interpolate 的结果上调用 model(x,t)
将模型速度与 cfm_target 的元素平方误差取平均
```

`interpolate` 和 `cfm_target` 保持端点张量的形状与 dtype。`cfm_loss` 返回一个标量，平均必须覆盖 batch 和所有坐标，并保留模型参数的梯度。

`sample_t` 与 `euler_sample` 已提供。测试 harness 管理模型、优化器和训练循环，训练时会调用你的 `cfm_loss`。默认时间均匀采样；辅助函数里的 logit-normal 选项供后续比较。

## 4. 本题约定

| 项目 | 本模块约定 |
| --- | --- |
| 端点 | `x0` 是噪声，`x1` 是数据 |
| 时间 | `t` 为 `[B]`，从 0 走向 1 |
| 条件路径 | 采用论文条件 OT 路径在终端噪声为零时的形式 |
| 配对 | 独立噪声与数据配对 |
| 损失归约 | 对 batch 及所有坐标取平均 |
| 测试模型 | `model(x,t)` 返回与 x 同形状的速度 |

由条件目标回归学到的是边缘速度场，无需为每个训练样本求解整条 ODE。

## 5. 交互可视化

<viz id="flow_particles" />

播放粒子流动并拖动时间，查看当前位置的速度场箭头。切换 Euler 步数，比较直线 oracle 与学习到的弯曲轨迹。

<viz id="convention_bug" />

切换反向采样错误，观察同一模型如何生成错误结果；同时查看 loss 曲线，理解 loss 下降不足以证明采样正确。

## 6. 在网页中运行

在右侧 Python 编辑器中补全实现，点击 **运行测试**。查看失败测试的原因、期望值与实际值，修改代码后再次运行。所有必要测试通过后，题目会标记为已完成并解锁坑点讲解。

## 7. 延伸

提供的 Euler 求解器沿时间递增积分，在左端点求值以避开单点 oracle 的 t=1 奇点：

$$x_{k+1}=x_k+\frac1n v_\theta(x_k,k/n),\quad k=0,\ldots,n-1.$$

可进一步阅读 [Rectified Flow](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.03003) 的重新耦合，以及 [SD3 式 13](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.03206v1) 的反向时间约定与非均匀时间采样。这些比较属于拓展，不增加本模块的必做函数。
problems.notes:
# 通过后的复盘

- 插值、目标符号、积分方向必须一致。`test_point_zero_loss` 检查训练，`test_gaussian_transport` 与 `test_learns_eight_modes` 检查生成，避免只看 loss 下降。
- 单点 oracle 在 t=1 有奇点；Euler 用左端点求值，最大时间是 (n-1)/n。`test_no_singular_endpoint` 直接记录调用时间。
- 条件目标有不可约方差，CFM loss 通常不能降到零。`test_point_zero_loss` 的特殊单点数据才具有零最优误差；真实训练曲线保留非零终值。
- 本题 loss 是所有 batch 和坐标元素取平均；与对坐标求和再对 batch 平均相差维度因子，`test_reference` 明确这一约定。
- 2000 步 TimeMLP 并非完美 oracle：半径 .5 的离群率实测 .123，阈值按规格规则取 ×1.5=.1845，MMD 也按 ×1.5 标定，并单独要求八模式均覆盖、每模式占比距 .125 不超过 .05。具体环境和数值在 problem.yaml；该阈值针对短训练预算，并不等同 DDPM 反向去噪模块的精确 oracle 质量。

时间方向已核对 [Lipman 式 22–23](https://arxiv.org/html/2210.02747v2)、[Rectified Flow](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.03003)、[SD3 式 13](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.03206v1)，访问日期 2026-10-13。

en.title: Conditional Path and Velocity Regression
en.readme:
# Conditional Path and Velocity Regression

## 1. What the paper solves

Flow Matching learns a time-dependent velocity field that transports noise into data through an ordinary differential equation. Its conditional training objective regresses a directly computable velocity, without simulating an entire generation trajectory on every training step.

This module selects the linear conditional path and its CFM objective. Implement only `interpolate`, `cfm_target`, and `cfm_loss`; time sampling, the Euler solver, test model, and training loop are supplied.

## 2. Core equations

In this exercise, x0 is noise and x1 is data. Both have shape `[B,D]`; time t has shape `[B]`, with a separate interpolation weight for each sample:

$$x_t=(1-t)x_0+tx_1,\qquad u=x_1-x_0,\qquad\mathcal L=\operatorname{mean}_{b,d}\left(v_\theta(x_t,t)-u\right)^2.$$

The conditional velocity u is the displacement between a pair of endpoints, but the network sees only the current position and time. Different endpoint pairs can reach the same position, so the network learns an average conditional velocity. Even an optimal network generally has nonzero training loss: irreducible variance is not an implementation error. See [Flow Matching Equations 5, 9, 22, and 23](https://arxiv.org/html/2210.02747v2) for gradient equivalence and linear conditional paths.

A point distribution is a special case: $v^*(x,t)=(\mu-x)/(1-t)$. Substituting the interpolated position gives a constant target velocity, zero oracle loss, and exact arrival at the data point in one Euler step. Marginal trajectories for general mixtures can curve, making multiple integration steps useful.

## 3. From equations to code

Implement three functions around the same training objective:

```text
interpolate: broadcast t [B] to [B,...] and construct the noise-to-data path
cfm_target: return the path’s derivative with respect to time
cfm_loss: evaluate model(x,t) at the result of interpolate
Average the squared elementwise error against cfm_target
```

`interpolate` and `cfm_target` preserve endpoint shape and dtype. `cfm_loss` returns a scalar, averages over the batch and every coordinate, and preserves gradients to model parameters.

`sample_t` and `euler_sample` are provided. The test harness manages the model, optimizer, and training loop, calling your `cfm_loss` during training. Time sampling is uniform by default; the helper’s logit-normal option is available for later comparison.

## 4. Conventions

| Item | This module’s convention |
| --- | --- |
| Endpoints | `x0` is noise; `x1` is data |
| Time | `t` has shape `[B]` and runs from 0 to 1 |
| Conditional path | The paper’s conditional OT path with zero terminal noise |
| Pairing | Independent noise and data |
| Loss reduction | Mean over the batch and every coordinate |
| Test model | `model(x,t)` returns a velocity with the same shape as x |

Regression against conditional targets learns the marginal velocity field, without solving an ODE for each training example.

## 5. Interactive visualizations

<viz id="flow_particles" />

Play the particle flow and move through time to inspect velocity arrows at current positions. Change Euler step counts to compare straight oracle paths with learned curved trajectories.

<viz id="convention_bug" />

Toggle the reversed-sampling bug to see the same model generate incorrect results. Compare the loss curve to understand why decreasing training loss alone does not establish correct sampling.

## 6. Run your implementation

Complete the functions in the Python editor on the right, then click **Run tests**. Inspect each failed check, update your implementation, and run again. Passing every required check marks the problem as solved and unlocks the notes.

## 7. Further exploration

The supplied Euler solver integrates forward in time, evaluating at left endpoints to avoid the point oracle’s singularity at t=1:

$$x_{k+1}=x_k+\frac1n v_\theta(x_k,k/n),\quad k=0,\ldots,n-1.$$

For optional exploration, read [Rectified Flow](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.03003) on recoupling and [SD3 Equation 13](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.03206v1) on reversed time conventions and nonuniform time sampling. These comparisons add no required functions to this module.
en.notes:
# Flow Matching: Review after passing

- Interpolation, target sign, and integration direction must agree. `test_point_zero_loss` checks training; `test_gaussian_transport` and `test_learns_eight_modes` check generation, rather than relying only on decreasing loss.
- The point-distribution oracle is singular at t=1. Euler evaluates left endpoints, so its largest evaluation time is (n-1)/n. `test_no_singular_endpoint` records the actual call times.
- Conditional targets have irreducible variance, so CFM loss generally cannot reach zero. Only the special point distribution in `test_point_zero_loss` has zero optimal error; the real training curves retain a nonzero final loss.
- The loss averages over every batch and coordinate element. Summing over coordinates before averaging over the batch differs by the number of dimensions. `test_reference` makes this contract explicit.
- A TimeMLP trained for 2,000 steps is not an exact oracle. The measured outlier fraction beyond radius .5 is .123; the specification's factor of 1.5 gives a threshold of .1845. MMD is calibrated by the same factor. Separately, all eight modes must be covered and each mode's share must be within .05 of .125. Environment details and measurements are in `problem.yaml`. These thresholds apply to a short training budget and do not imply the exact-oracle quality used in problem **8**.

The original exercise checked the time conventions against [Lipman Equations 22–23](https://arxiv.org/html/2210.02747v2), [Rectified Flow](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.03003), and [SD3 Equation 13](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.03206v1) on 2026-10-13.

problems.readme:
# GSPO 序列比率与截断

实现序列重要性比率和截断策略损失。

论文：[Group Sequence Policy Optimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.18071v1)。定位：Section 4.1, Eqs. (6–8): sequence objective and geometric importance ratio；Section 4.2, Eq. (11): equal token gradient weights。

## 精选核心

只实现两个函数；组 advantage 计算、采样和分布式 RL 不属于本模块。

$$
s_i=\exp\left(\frac{\sum_t m_{it}(\log\pi_{it}-\log\pi^{old}_{it})}{\sum_t m_{it}}\right)
$$

- `sequence_ratio(logp: Tensor, old_logp: Tensor, mask: Tensor) -> Tensor`
- `gspo_loss(logp: Tensor, old_logp: Tensor, advantages: Tensor, mask: Tensor, clip_eps: float=0.2) -> Tensor`

## 接口与实验

`logp`、`old_logp`、二元 `mask` 形状为 `[B,L]`，`advantages` 为 `[B]`。先对有效 log-ratio 求和、除以有效长度，再取指数。每个回答只截断这个序列比率，与冻结 advantage 相乘取较小项，最后对 batch 求负均值。

旧策略与 advantage 不参与梯度。全 padding 回答比率为 1、损失贡献为 0，仍计入 batch 大小。必须在指数运算前屏蔽 padding。重复一个回答内部的 token 不改变结果。本题实现 GSPO，不是 GSPO-token。默认 `.2` 截断是便于观察的教学设置，不代表 Qwen 生产训练参数。

实验使用 token 比率 `[2, 0.5]`，它们的几何比率为 1，两个有效 log-probability 的梯度相同。正 advantage 的比率 1.5 和负 advantage 的比率 0.5 均被截断。产物保存学员实现计算的比率和梯度矩阵。

## Toy 来源

**PaperLeet 教学改编。** PaperLeet 自编的三回答解析实验，不是 Qwen 训练结果。 判题 harness 调用本次提交的函数，保存由其产生的指标与曲线。Lab 静态预览来自参考实现，Run/Submit 的产物来自你的代码。`experiment.py` 与 `tests/` 已提供实验和判题脚手架。

## 来源与验证

[作者说明（尚未验证作者训练代码发布）](https://qwenlm.github.io/blog/gspo/)。题目实现与合成数据由 PaperLeet 编写；论文链接固定公式依据的版本。

T0 验证接口，T1 对照参考值，T2 检查数学性质与梯度，T3 用你的实现运行 toy。在在线编辑器补全 starter 后 Run 或 Submit，无需部署完整大模型训练系统。

problems.solution:
import torch
from torch import Tensor


def sequence_ratio(logp: Tensor, old_logp: Tensor, mask: Tensor) -> Tensor:
    """Length-normalized sequence importance weights, [B,L] -> [B]."""
    delta = torch.where(mask.bool(), logp - old_logp.detach(), torch.zeros_like(logp))
    lengths = mask.sum(-1).clamp_min(1)
    return (delta.sum(-1) / lengths).exp()


def gspo_loss(logp: Tensor, old_logp: Tensor, advantages: Tensor,
              mask: Tensor, clip_eps: float = 0.2) -> Tensor:
    """Sequence clipping; empty responses contribute zero to the batch mean."""
    ratio = sequence_ratio(logp, old_logp, mask)
    advantage = advantages.detach()
    objective = torch.minimum(ratio * advantage,
                              ratio.clamp(1 - clip_eps, 1 + clip_eps) * advantage)
    return -(objective * mask.bool().any(-1)).mean()
problems.notes:
# 实现说明 — GSPO 序列比率与截断

`logp`、`old_logp`、二元 `mask` 形状为 `[B,L]`，`advantages` 为 `[B]`。先对有效 log-ratio 求和、除以有效长度，再取指数。每个回答只截断这个序列比率，与冻结 advantage 相乘取较小项，最后对 batch 求负均值。

旧策略与 advantage 不参与梯度。全 padding 回答比率为 1、损失贡献为 0，仍计入 batch 大小。必须在指数运算前屏蔽 padding。重复一个回答内部的 token 不改变结果。本题实现 GSPO，不是 GSPO-token。默认 `.2` 截断是便于观察的教学设置，不代表 Qwen 生产训练参数。

实验使用 token 比率 `[2, 0.5]`，它们的几何比率为 1，两个有效 log-probability 的梯度相同。正 advantage 的比率 1.5 和负 advantage 的比率 0.5 均被截断。产物保存学员实现计算的比率和梯度矩阵。

## 错误变体

- 对 token 比率做算术平均，误把几何序列比率改成算术均值。
- 遗漏回答长度归一化。
- 错误地向采样旧策略传播梯度。
- 截断代理目标错误取最大值。

每个 mutant 都是相对于参考实现的小幅故意错误。T2 包含独立公式或梯度期望，接受结果不只依赖参考值相等。T3 使用传入的学员实现产生结果。

en.title: GSPO Sequence Ratios and Clipping
en.readme:
# GSPO Sequence Ratios and Clipping

Implement the sequence importance ratio and clipped policy loss.

Paper: [Group Sequence Policy Optimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.18071v1). Anchors: Section 4.1, Eqs. (6–8): sequence objective and geometric importance ratio; Section 4.2, Eq. (11): equal token gradient weights.

## Selected core

Two functions; group advantages, sampling and distributed RL are outside this module.

$$
s_i=\exp\left(\frac{\sum_t m_{it}(\log\pi_{it}-\log\pi^{old}_{it})}{\sum_t m_{it}}\right)
$$

- `sequence_ratio(logp: Tensor, old_logp: Tensor, mask: Tensor) -> Tensor`
- `gspo_loss(logp: Tensor, old_logp: Tensor, advantages: Tensor, mask: Tensor, clip_eps: float=0.2) -> Tensor`

## Contract and experiment

`logp`, `old_logp`, and binary `mask` have shape `[B,L]`; `advantages` has shape `[B]`. First sum the valid log-ratios and divide by valid length, then exponentiate. Clip that single ratio per response, multiply by the detached advantage, take the smaller surrogate, and negate the batch mean.

The old policy and advantages are frozen. A response with no valid tokens has ratio 1 and contributes zero to the batch mean. Padding must be neutralized **before** exponentiation, including extreme padded scores. Duplicating tokens within a response leaves the loss unchanged. This module implements GSPO, not GSPO-token. The default `.2` clip is an inspectable teaching setting; it is not a claim about Qwen's production hyperparameter.

Try token ratios `[2, 0.5]`: their geometric ratio is 1, so both valid log-probabilities receive the same gradient. A positive-advantage response with ratio 1.5 clips; a negative-advantage response with ratio 0.5 also clips. The toy saves the submitted implementation's ratios and gradient matrix.

## Toy provenance

**PaperLeet teaching adaptation.** Analytic three-response diagnostic written for PaperLeet; not Qwen training results. The test harness calls your submitted functions and records the resulting metrics and curves. The Lab's static preview comes from the reference; your Run/Submit artifacts come from your code. The experiment and test scaffolding are supplied in `experiment.py` and `tests/`.

## Sources and verification

[Author explanation (no author training-code release verified)](https://qwenlm.github.io/blog/gspo/). All exercise implementations and synthetic data are written for PaperLeet. The paper link pins the version used for the formulas.

T0 checks contracts, T1 compares with the reference, T2 checks mathematical and gradient properties, and T3 runs the toy through your implementation. Implement the starter functions in the online editor, then Run or Submit. The official large-model training system is not required.
en.notes:
# Implementation notes — GSPO Sequence Ratios and Clipping

`logp`, `old_logp`, and binary `mask` have shape `[B,L]`; `advantages` has shape `[B]`. First sum the valid log-ratios and divide by valid length, then exponentiate. Clip that single ratio per response, multiply by the detached advantage, take the smaller surrogate, and negate the batch mean.

The old policy and advantages are frozen. A response with no valid tokens has ratio 1 and contributes zero to the batch mean. Padding must be neutralized **before** exponentiation, including extreme padded scores. Duplicating tokens within a response leaves the loss unchanged. This module implements GSPO, not GSPO-token. The default `.2` clip is an inspectable teaching setting; it is not a claim about Qwen's production hyperparameter.

Try token ratios `[2, 0.5]`: their geometric ratio is 1, so both valid log-probabilities receive the same gradient. A positive-advantage response with ratio 1.5 clips; a negative-advantage response with ratio 0.5 also clips. The toy saves the submitted implementation's ratios and gradient matrix.

## Deliberately wrong variants

- Average token ratios instead of the geometric sequence ratio.
- Omit response-length normalization.
- Backpropagate into the behavior policy.
- Maximize instead of minimize clipped surrogate.

Each mutant differs from the reference in a small, intentional change. T2 includes independent formula or gradient expectations, so equality with the reference is not the only acceptance evidence. T3 produces artifacts from the supplied implementation.

# 学生前缀上的 On-policy Distillation

从学生分布采样，在相同前缀上蒸馏教师全词表反馈。

论文：[On-policy Distillation of Language Models: Learning from Self-Generated Mistakes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.13649v3)。定位：Section 3, Algorithm 1: GKD and student data fraction lambda；Section 3, Eqs. (2–4): token divergences on student-generated prefixes；Appendix A.7: forward/reverse KL interpretation (separate conceptual example)。

## 精选核心

选取 GKD 的 lambda=1 与明确方向的 KL；提供三 token Markov 语言模型代替大型语言模型。

$$
L=\mathbb E_{y\sim p_S}[\frac1{|y|}\sum_t D_{KL}(p_S(\cdot|y_{<t})\Vert p_T(\cdot|y_{<t}))]
$$

- `sample_student(transition_logits: Tensor, batch_size: int, length: int, generator: torch.Generator) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]`
- `distillation_loss(student_logits: Tensor, teacher_logits: Tensor, mask: Tensor, direction: str='reverse') -> Tensor`

## 接口与实验

en.readme:
# On-policy Distillation at Student Prefixes

Sample from the student and distill full-vocabulary feedback at the same prefixes.

Paper: [On-policy Distillation of Language Models: Learning from Self-Generated Mistakes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.13649v3). Anchors: Section 3, Algorithm 1: GKD and student data fraction lambda; Section 3, Eqs. (2–4): token divergences on student-generated prefixes; Appendix A.7: forward/reverse KL interpretation (separate conceptual example).

## Selected core

GKD with lambda=1 and explicit forward/reverse KL; a supplied three-token Markov LM replaces large language models.

$$
L=\mathbb E_{y\sim p_S}[\frac1{|y|}\sum_t D_{KL}(p_S(\cdot|y_{<t})\Vert p_T(\cdot|y_{<t}))]
$$

- `sample_student(transition_logits: Tensor, batch_size: int, length: int, generator: torch.Generator) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]`
- `distillation_loss(student_logits: Tensor, teacher_logits: Tensor, mask: Tensor, direction: str='reverse') -> Tensor`

## Contract and experiment

Implement `sample_student` and `distillation_loss`. The sampling table has shape `[V+1,V]`; row `V` is BOS and row `k` is the distribution after token `k`. Return `(tokens, prefixes)`, both `[B,L]` integer tensors. The first prefix is BOS; every subsequent prefix is the previous sampled token. Use the supplied generator and categorical sampling at temperature 1, without a gradient through discrete sampling. Sequences have fixed length and no EOS in this toy.

The loss inputs are `[B,L,V]` logits evaluated for **both models at those same student-generated prefixes**, plus `[B,L]` binary mask. `reverse` means KL(student || teacher); `forward` means KL(teacher || student). Sum over the entire vocabulary, average only valid tokens, freeze the teacher, and use log-softmax. All-padding gives differentiable zero. Padded logits may be nonfinite and must be neutralized before log-softmax. Valid logits are finite.

This is the lambda=1 GKD variant. It is not sampled-token OPD, a policy-gradient estimator, or teacher-generated training data. The supplied training loop learns four conditional distributions with a three-token model. Its evaluation metric is mean forward KL over all four states, while the training objective is reverse KL on fresh student prefixes.

## Toy provenance

**PaperLeet teaching adaptation.** PaperLeet fixed-length categorical Markov model, not the original T5 or Gaussian-mixture experiment. The test harness calls your submitted functions and records the resulting metrics and curves. The Lab's static preview comes from the reference; your Run/Submit artifacts come from your code. The experiment and test scaffolding are supplied in `experiment.py` and `tests/`.

## Sources and verification

[TRL implementation (independent of the paper authors; not the reference for this exercise)](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/main/trl/experimental/gkd/gkd_trainer.py). All exercise implementations and synthetic data are written for PaperLeet. The paper link pins the version used for the formulas.

T0 checks contracts, T1 compares with the reference, T2 checks mathematical and gradient properties, and T3 runs the toy through your implementation. Implement the starter functions in the online editor, then Run or Submit. The official large-model training system is not required.

# DAPO 动态筛选与 Token 目标

筛选有效组，实现非对称的按 token 归一化截断目标。

论文：[DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14476v1)。定位：Section 3, Eqs. (8–11): token normalization, asymmetric clipping and dynamic sampling；Sections 3.1–3.3; Section 4.1 clip_low=.2 and clip_high=.28。

## 精选核心

两个有界核心函数；不复现超采样调度、超长奖励整形和分布式训练。

$$
L=-\frac{\sum_{i,t}m_{it}\min(r_{it}A_i,\mathrm{clip}(r_{it},1-\epsilon_l,1+\epsilon_h)A_i)}{\sum_{i,t}m_{it}}
$$

- `dynamic_group_mask(rewards: Tensor) -> Tensor`
- `dapo_loss(logp: Tensor, old_logp: Tensor, advantages: Tensor, mask: Tensor, clip_low: float=0.2, clip_high: float=0.28) -> Tensor`

## 接口与实验

`dynamic_group_mask` 输入二元结果奖励 `[prompts,group]`，组大小至少为 2。输出 `[prompts]` 布尔向量，仅保留同时有成功与失败的组。支持 `0/1` 和 `-1/1` 编码。筛选是动态采样的核心原语，生产采样器还需继续补满 batch。

`dapo_loss` 输入 `[B,L]` 当前/旧 log-probability、二元 mask 和 `[B]` 已归一化 advantage。调用者已筛选这些回答。冻结旧分数与 advantage，独立使用上下界，按**全 batch 有效 token 总数**归一化，不能先求回答内均值。默认上下宽度为 `.2/.28`，不添加参考策略 KL。空 mask 返回可微零，指数前屏蔽极端 padding。

Toy 在全错、混合、全对三个组中只保留混合组，然后扫描 .5 至 1.5 的比率。正 advantage 的 1.25 比率在上界宽度 .28 时仍应有梯度；测试另检查不同回答长度的权重。

problems.solution:
import torch
from torch import Tensor


def dynamic_group_mask(rewards: Tensor) -> Tensor:
    """[prompts,group] binary rewards (0/1 or -1/1) -> informative prompts."""
    if rewards.ndim != 2 or rewards.shape[-1] < 2:
        raise ValueError('rewards must have shape [prompts, group >= 2]')
    return rewards.max(-1).values > rewards.min(-1).values


def dapo_loss(logp: Tensor, old_logp: Tensor, advantages: Tensor, mask: Tensor,
              clip_low: float = 0.2, clip_high: float = 0.28) -> Tensor:
    """Asymmetric clipping, averaged over all retained response tokens."""
    delta = torch.where(mask.bool(), logp - old_logp.detach(), torch.zeros_like(logp))
    ratio = delta.exp()
    advantage = advantages.detach().unsqueeze(-1)
    objective = torch.minimum(ratio * advantage,
                              ratio.clamp(1 - clip_low, 1 + clip_high) * advantage)
    return -(objective * mask).sum() / mask.sum().clamp_min(1)

# LoRA 低秩更新与冻结基座前向

实现缩放低秩更新并冻结基座参数。

论文：[LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685v2)。定位：Section 4.1, Eq. (3): W0 + BA and alpha/r scaling；Section 4.1: random A, zero B initialization and merged inference。

## 精选核心

实现线性层的两个函数；初始化与 rank-2 回归训练循环已提供。

$$
y=xW_0^\top+\frac\alpha r xA^\top B^\top
$$

- `lora_delta(a: Tensor, b: Tensor, alpha: float=1.0) -> Tensor`
- `lora_linear(x: Tensor, weight: Tensor, a: Tensor, b: Tensor, alpha: float=1.0, bias: Tensor | None=None) -> Tensor`

## 接口与实验

实现 `lora_delta(A,B,alpha)` 与 `lora_linear(x,W,A,B,alpha,bias)`。形状为 `A[r,in]`、`B[out,r]`、`W[out,in]`、`x[...,in]`。增量为 `(alpha/r) * B @ A`。前向等于冻结基座线性映射加低秩更新。即使输入基座权重与 bias 的 `requires_grad=True`，也不能向它们传播梯度；`x`、`A`、`B` 的梯度必须保留。

训练脚手架随机初始化 A、零初始化 B。因此初始输出不变，B 有学习信号而 A 的首次梯度为零。对整个基座计算使用 `no_grad()` 会错误删除部分 x 梯度。将 delta 加到 W 即可合并，测试比较合并前后结果。本模块不包含 dropout。

Toy 冻结一个 6×8 映射，用 28 个 adapter 参数拟合已知 rank-2 变化。平台提供输入、优化器和 300 步 CPU 训练。通过表示恢复这个可控目标，不是复现完整语言模型指标。

## Toy 来源

**PaperLeet 教学改编。** PaperLeet rank-2 合成回归，不是语言模型基准。 判题 harness 调用本次提交的函数，保存由其产生的指标与曲线。Lab 静态预览来自参考实现，Run/Submit 的产物来自你的代码。`experiment.py` 与 `tests/` 已提供实验和判题脚手架。

## 来源与验证

[微软 LoRA 官方实现](https://github.com/microsoft/LoRA/blob/main/loralib/layers.py)。题目实现与合成数据由 PaperLeet 编写；论文链接固定公式依据的版本。

en.readme:
# LoRA Low-rank Updates and Frozen-base Forward

Implement a scaled low-rank update while freezing base parameters.

Paper: [LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685v2). Anchors: Section 4.1, Eq. (3): W0 + BA and alpha/r scaling; Section 4.1: random A, zero B initialization and merged inference.

## Selected core

Two functions for a linear layer; initialization and a rank-two regression training loop are provided.

$$
y=xW_0^\top+\frac\alpha r xA^\top B^\top
$$

- `lora_delta(a: Tensor, b: Tensor, alpha: float=1.0) -> Tensor`
- `lora_linear(x: Tensor, weight: Tensor, a: Tensor, b: Tensor, alpha: float=1.0, bias: Tensor | None=None) -> Tensor`

## Contract and experiment

Implement `lora_delta(A,B,alpha)` and `lora_linear(x,W,A,B,alpha,bias)`. Shapes are `A[r,in]`, `B[out,r]`, `W[out,in]`, and `x[...,in]`. The delta is `(alpha/r) * B @ A`. The forward operation is the frozen base linear map plus this low-rank update. Base weight and optional bias must not receive gradients, even when their inputs have `requires_grad=True`; gradients to `x`, `A`, and `B` must remain intact.

The training scaffold initializes A randomly and B to zero. Initially, the adapter changes no outputs: B has a nonzero learning signal while A's first gradient is zero. Freezing the entire base computation with `no_grad()` would incorrectly remove part of the gradient to x. Merge by adding the returned delta to W; the exercise compares merged and unmerged outputs. There is no dropout in this module.

The toy freezes a 6-by-8 map and fits a known rank-two change using 28 adapter parameters. The platform supplies input data, optimizer and 300 CPU training steps. Passing means recovering this controlled target, not reproducing a full language-model benchmark.

## Toy provenance

**PaperLeet teaching adaptation.** PaperLeet rank-two synthetic regression, not a language-model benchmark. The test harness calls your submitted functions and records the resulting metrics and curves. The Lab's static preview comes from the reference; your Run/Submit artifacts come from your code. The experiment and test scaffolding are supplied in `experiment.py` and `tests/`.

## Sources and verification

[Official Microsoft LoRA implementation](https://github.com/microsoft/LoRA/blob/main/loralib/layers.py). All exercise implementations and synthetic data are written for PaperLeet. The paper link pins the version used for the formulas.

T0 checks contracts, T1 compares with the reference, T2 checks mathematical and gradient properties, and T3 runs the toy through your implementation. Implement the starter functions in the online editor, then Run or Submit. The official large-model training system is not required.

problems.solution:
import torch
from torch import Tensor


# NF4 levels from bitsandbytes 0.43.3 get_4bit_type('nf4'). Zero is index 7.
NF4 = (-1.0, -0.6961928009986877, -0.5250730514526367, -0.39491748809814453,
       -0.28444138169288635, -0.18477343022823334, -0.09105003625154495, 0.0,
       0.07958029955625534, 0.16093020141124725, 0.24611230194568634,
       0.33791524171829224, 0.44070982933044434, 0.5626170039176941,
       0.7229568362236023, 1.0)


def nf4_quantize(weight: Tensor, block_size: int = 64) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    """Unpacked uint8 code indices plus per-block absmax; last block may be short."""
    if block_size < 1 or weight.numel() == 0:
        raise ValueError('positive block_size and a nonempty weight are required')
    flat = weight.detach().reshape(-1)
    levels = weight.new_tensor(NF4)
    codes, scales = [], []
    for block in flat.split(block_size):
        scale = block.abs().max()
        normalized = block / torch.where(scale > 0, scale, torch.ones_like(scale))
        codes.append((normalized[:, None] - levels).abs().argmin(-1).to(torch.uint8))
        scales.append(scale)
    return torch.cat(codes).reshape_as(weight), torch.stack(scales)


def nf4_dequantize(codes: Tensor, scales: Tensor, block_size: int = 64) -> Tensor:
    """Frozen block scales; output shape matches codes, dtype/device follow scales."""
    if block_size < 1 or codes.numel() == 0 or scales.numel() != (codes.numel() + block_size - 1) // block_size:
        raise ValueError('one scale is required for each nonempty block')
    levels = scales.new_tensor(NF4)
    block_scales = scales.detach().reshape(-1).repeat_interleave(block_size)[:codes.numel()]
    return (levels[codes.long().reshape(-1)] * block_scales).reshape_as(codes)


def qlora_linear(x: Tensor, codes: Tensor, scales: Tensor, a: Tensor, b: Tensor,
                 alpha: float = 1.0, block_size: int = 64, bias: Tensor | None = None) -> Tensor:
    """Dequantized frozen base plus a differentiable alpha/r low-rank adapter."""
    weight = nf4_dequantize(codes, scales, block_size).to(dtype=x.dtype)
    base = torch.nn.functional.linear(x, weight, None if bias is None else bias.detach())
    return base + ((x @ a.T) @ b.T) * (alpha / a.shape[0])

en.readme:
# QLoRA NF4 Blocks and Trainable Adapters

Implement block NF4 quantization and train adapters through a frozen quantized base.

Paper: [QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14314v1). Anchors: Section 3: NormalFloat4 and frozen quantized base with LoRA; Appendix E: asymmetric NF4 with exact zero; bitsandbytes 0.43.3 functional.py get_4bit_type: pinned 16-level NF4 codebook.

## Selected core

Three CPU functions. Code indices are unpacked uint8 for inspectability; packed 4-bit storage, double quantization and paged optimizers are outside scope.

$$
W\approx s_b C_{q(W/s_b)},\qquad y=x\mathrm{dequant}(W)^\top+\frac\alpha r xA^\top B^\top
$$

- `nf4_quantize(weight: Tensor, block_size: int=64) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]`
- `nf4_dequantize(codes: Tensor, scales: Tensor, block_size: int=64) -> Tensor`
- `qlora_linear(x: Tensor, codes: Tensor, scales: Tensor, a: Tensor, b: Tensor, alpha: float=1.0, block_size: int=64, bias: Tensor | None=None) -> Tensor`

## Contract and experiment

Implement block quantization, dequantization and a frozen-base adapter forward. The **provided `NF4` tuple** is the pinned asymmetric 16-value codebook: exact zero is index 7, positive and negative nonzero levels are not mirror images. Flatten the weight in row-major order, split into blocks, divide by each block's absmax, and choose the nearest level. Ties choose the lower code index. A zero block has scale zero and all code indices 7. A final short block has its own scale.

Return uint8 **unpacked indices** with the original weight shape and a flat floating-point scale vector. Decoding repeats each scale for its block. Weight quantization is frozen; dequantization freezes scales. # Implementation notes — QLoRA NF4 Blocks and Trainable Adapters

Implement block quantization, dequantization and a frozen-base adapter forward. The **provided `NF4` tuple** is the pinned asymmetric 16-value codebook: exact zero is index 7, positive and negative nonzero levels are not mirror images. Flatten the weight in row-major order, split into blocks, divide by each block's absmax, and choose the nearest level. Ties choose the lower code index. A zero block has scale zero and all code indices 7. A final short block has its own scale.

Return uint8 **unpacked indices** with the original weight shape and a flat floating-point scale vector. Decoding repeats each scale for its block. Weight quantization is frozen; dequantization freezes scales. The forward accepts A[r,in], B[out,r] and alpha/r scaling, preserves input/adapter gradients and freezes optional bias. `block_size` defaults to 64; tests use smaller blocks for inspection. NF4 constants are supplied in the starter; they are not something to memorize.

The toy trains adapters on a frozen quantized map. Storage here consumes one byte per index, not half a byte. It intentionally omits nibble packing, double quantization, paged optimizers and CUDA kernels, so its metrics cannot establish the paper's full memory claims. See the [official QLoRA training repository](https://github.com/artidoro/qlora) for those larger-system components.

## Deliberately wrong variants

- Replace NF4 with uniform levels.
- Use global absmax for each block.
- Allow gradients into frozen scales.
- Forget adapter rank normalization.

Each mutant differs from the reference in a small, intentional change. T2 includes independent formula or gradient expectations, so equality with the reference is not the only acceptance evidence. T3 produces artifacts from the supplied implementation.

problems.solution:
import math
import torch
from torch import Tensor


def _time(t: Tensor, x: Tensor) -> Tensor:
    return t.reshape(-1, *([1] * (x.ndim - 1)))


def drift_field(generated: Tensor, positive: Tensor, temperature: float = .2) -> Tensor:
    """Official toy's doubly normalized distance kernel; generated self-pairs masked."""
    if not math.isfinite(temperature) or temperature <= 0:
        raise ValueError('temperature must be positive and finite')
    if len(generated) == 0 or len(positive) == 0:
        raise ValueError('both sample sets must be nonempty')
    n = len(generated)
    targets = torch.cat((generated, positive))
    distance = torch.cdist(generated, targets)
    mask = torch.cat((torch.eye(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=generated.device), torch.zeros(n, len(positive), dtype=torch.bool, device=generated.device)), dim=1)
    log_kernel = (-distance / temperature).masked_fill(mask, -torch.inf)
    row_mass = torch.logsumexp(log_kernel, dim=1, keepdim=True)
    column_mass = torch.logsumexp(log_kernel, dim=0, keepdim=True)
    # A column containing only the masked self-pair has zero affinity.
    column_mass = torch.where(torch.isfinite(column_mass), column_mass, torch.zeros_like(column_mass))
    log_normalizer = .5 * (row_mass + column_mass)
    affinity = torch.exp(log_kernel - log_normalizer)
    negative, positive_weight = affinity[:, :n], affinity[:, n:]
    attraction = (positive_weight @ positive) * negative.sum(1, keepdim=True)
    repulsion = (negative @ generated) * positive_weight.sum(1, keepdim=True)
    return attraction - repulsion


def drifting_loss(generated: Tensor, positive: Tensor, temperature: float = .2) -> Tensor:
    """MSE(g, stopgrad(g + V)); gradients flow only through the left-hand g."""
    field = drift_field(generated.detach(), positive.detach(), temperature)
    target = (generated + field).detach()
    return (generated - target).square().mean()

# 18. Drifting: Pairwise Field and Frozen Targets

Implement the distance-kernel drifting field and its stop-gradient target; train a generator with one-pass inference.

## Contract

- `drift_field(generated: Tensor, positive: Tensor, temperature: float = .2) -> Tensor`
- `drifting_loss(generated: Tensor, positive: Tensor, temperature: float = .2) -> Tensor`

The field uses exp(-Euclidean distance/temperature), masks generated self-pairs, normalizes by sqrt(row_mass*column_mass), and combines positive and negative weighted centers with their opposite group masses. This selects the official toy variant, not a generic attraction-only field. The whole g+V target is frozen; removing this detach can preserve the scalar loss while making the gradient zero. One-step means generator inference, not one training update.

# 19. DMD: Score-Difference Distillation

- `dmd_loss(generated: Tensor, gradient: Tensor, paired_target: Tensor, regression_weight: float = .1) -> Tensor`
- `fake_score_loss(model, generated: Tensor, noise: Tensor, sigma: Tensor) -> Tensor`

# 20. DMD2: Two-Time-Scale and Adversarial Updates

Implement the critic-to-generator update ratio and non-saturating GAN contribution on top of distribution matching.

## Contract

- `generator_due(completed_critic_updates: int, critic_per_generator: int = 5) -> bool`
- `adversarial_losses(real_logits: Tensor, fake_logits: Tensor) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]`
- `generator_loss(generated: Tensor, gradient: Tensor, fake_logits: Tensor, gan_weight: float = .1) -> Tensor`

The critic/fake diffusion model updates more often than the generator (5:1 here). Counts are completed critic updates, so update 0 does not trigger a generator step. Logistic discriminator and generator losses have opposite signs on fake logits. Caller detaches fake data during critic training and freezes critic parameters, while retaining input gradients, during generator training. Unlike DMD, the generator objective has no paired teacher regression. This exercise covers the stabilization/real-data contribution, not the paper’s multistep backward simulation.

**Provenance: PaperLeet teaching adaptation.** An unpaired shifted-Gaussian toy jointly trains a fake score and discriminator for five updates per student update. It demonstrates scheduling, GAN gradient direction, and removal of paired regression. Uses scalar Gaussian score parameters rather than pretrained diffusion features.

en.readme:
# 21. Consistency Models: Boundary and Teacher Targets

Implement a boundary-preserving consistency function, stop-gradient pair loss, and EMA target update.

## Contract

- `consistency_function(model, noisy: Tensor, sigma: Tensor, sigma_min: float = .002, sigma_data: float = .5) -> Tensor`
- `consistency_loss(prediction: Tensor, target_prediction: Tensor) -> Tensor`
- `update_ema(online, target, decay: float = .95) -> None`
- `teacher_euler(noisy: Tensor, denoised: Tensor, sigma: Tensor, next_sigma: Tensor) -> Tensor` (provided)

At sigma_min the function must be exactly the identity, regardless of network output. The model receives c_in*x and the original sigma; this exercise supplies raw sigma conditioning instead of the official embedding. The skip/output coefficients follow the official boundary parameterization. The lower-noise teacher/EMA branch is frozen. The supplied Euler helper uses decreasing positive noise scales. This is consistency distillation with a teacher, not the separate teacher-free consistency-training algorithm.

## Runnable experiment

**Provenance: PaperLeet teaching adaptation.** A point-data teacher makes its probability-flow Euler step exact. Small MLP distillation exercises the boundary and target routing without pretrained models. Half the training pairs use a positive adjacent noise level sigma/2, so the EMA network affects the target; the other half anchor the exact sigma_min boundary.

The T3 test runs your submitted implementation, saves points/curves/metrics, and uses fixed seed 42. `toy.py` contains the provided experiment. It does not download models or datasets. These exercises reproduce selected mechanisms, not full image benchmark results.

problems.readme:
# 缩放点积注意力

Transformer 根据 query 与 key 的匹配程度，从 value 中汇聚信息。本题实现 [Attention Is All You Need §3.2.1、公式 (1)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762) 的核心算子。作者原始实现见 [Tensor2Tensor](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensor2tensor)。

## 核心任务

只需实现 `scaled_dot_product_attention`。`causal_mask` 与实验循环已经提供。输入已经完成投影并拆分 head；投影层、位置编码、前馈网络和完整语言模型训练不属于本题范围。

$$
S=QK^\top/\sqrt{d_k},\qquad A=\operatorname{softmax}_{\mathrm{keys}}(S+M),\qquad O=AV.
$$

可见位置的 mask 贡献为 0，不可见位置为负无穷。沿 **key 轴**分别对每个 query、每个 head 做稳定 softmax。返回输出 `O` 和权重 `A`，方便查看信息来自哪些位置。

| 输入或输出 | 约定 |
|---|---|
| `q`、`k`、`v` | `[B,H,Q,D]`、`[B,H,K,D]`、`[B,H,K,Dv]` |
| `mask` | 可广播至 `[B,H,Q,K]` 的布尔张量，`True` 表示可见 |
| 输出、权重 | `[B,H,Q,Dv]`、`[B,H,Q,K]`，保留精度与设备 |
| 全部屏蔽的 query | 输出和权重严格为 0，梯度有限且为 0 |
| 因果对齐 | 左上对齐：仅允许 `j <= i` 的 key |
| 范围 | 有限输入，无 dropout，允许 `D` 与 `Dv` 不同 |

全屏蔽行需要单独处理：直接对一整行负无穷做 softmax 会产生 NaN。先把这种行换成有限占位 logits，再将屏蔽位置的权重清零。这项 padding 约定是 PaperLeet 对论文公式的工程补充。

## 小例子

query 为 `[2,0,0,0]`，两个 key 为 `[1,0,0,0]`、`[0,0,0,0]` 时，缩放后的分数是 `[1,0]`，权重约为 `[0.7311,0.2689]`。若 mask 为 `[True,False]`，权重应为 `[1,0]`。

## Toy 实验

提供的**前缀平均**实验令全部 query/key 为零，再加入因果 mask。每个 query 的输出应恰好等于它目前见过的 value 的均值。把未来 value 增加 1000，前面的输出仍应不变。报告包含注意力矩阵、实际与期望前缀均值、未来信息泄漏量。

**来源：** PaperLeet 根据论文注意力与 mask 公式设计的教学改编，并非原论文实验。只用六个标量，不训练模型、不下载数据。T3 调用实际提交代码；实验室里的参考预览单独标记。

## 验证

T0 验证形状与输入未被修改。T1 使用可手算的两个 key。T2 验证广播 mask、空行、排列与平移不变性、独立梯度和因果隔离。T3 运行前缀平均实验。常见错误是遗漏平方根缩放、忽略 mask 或沿 query 轴归一化。

在编辑器中实现核心函数，再运行四层测试。完成本题表示掌握选定的 attention 核心，不等于复现完整 Transformer。
